title: Horror — Intermediate
summary: A deeper horror loop: shared sight and audio, dark interactions, a stalk that leaves its route, a creaking timeline, co-op limbs, keys and fuel, a fear effect, and a save that does not replay the creak.

sections.title: Stalker's senses
sections.why: Sight and a creak share Sense. Alert becomes 1 only on a clear trace.
reading: Intermediate horror keeps one Sense event. The excerpt starts it from Begin Play at 0.2 seconds, looping, traces, and assigns Alert = 1.f only when bHit is true. A closed door blocks the channel. A creak, a bottle, or a sprint calls Sense immediately, so audio is not waiting for the timer. The timer is the glimpse. The sound is the startle. They write the same float, which is why the stalk cannot disagree with itself.

A miss still does nothing in the sample. Add a decay on the else, a small subtract, or the hunter stays sure after the player hides. Do not move that decay to Tick. The else of this function is the miss. Co-op, if a second player exists, does not give the hunter a trace per client. The authority runs Sense once. Clients only hear the result if you replicate Alert.

The player's use trace must not write Alert. The fear effect later reads Alert. It does not trace. The door timeline emits the creak. Perception does not open the door. Save stores Alert after the decay, not mid-subtract.

sections.title: Fear as an effect
sections.why: OnEffect broadcasts when Alert stays high. ApplyEffect is a timer, not Tick.
reading: Fear is an effect the stalk can apply when Alert stays at 1. The excerpt binds OnEffect on Begin Play, starts a looping timer for ApplyEffect at 1 second, and the apply function broadcasts OnEffect. The UI and the camera shake bind to that dispatcher. They do not poll Alert. Tick that shakes the camera while Alert is high also shakes it for one frame after Alert decays, and it shakes during a pause if you are not careful.

The broadcast is the gameplay-ability shape: something applies, listeners hear. The hunter does not call the camera. Sense writes Alert. This timer reads it and broadcasts when the design says the fear should pulse. Putting the broadcast inside Sense would shake on every glimpse, including a 0.2 second peek the design wanted to forgive.

In co-op the effect runs on the authority and the broadcast can be local on each client from a replicated fear float. Broadcasting on every client from Tick duplicates the pulse. Save may store the fear float. It does not store the delegate bindings. Those are set up again in Begin Play.
